scenes.tts: Put a grid of electrodes on the retina. Do you get a grid of dots?
scenes.visual: Title card: Streaks and Pixels. A grid of electrodes beside a grid of dots, with a question mark between them.
scenes.narration: Put a grid of electrodes on the retina. Do you get a grid of dots?

scenes.tts: The Argus two tried it. A camera drove sixty electrodes on the inner surface of the retina.
scenes.caption: The Argus II tried it. A camera drove 60 electrodes on the inner surface of the retina.
scenes.visual: A camera on glasses; a 60-electrode array laid on the retina's inner surface. Label: epiretinal; da Cruz and colleagues, 2016.
scenes.narration: The Argus II tried it. A camera drove 60 electrodes on the inner surface of the retina.

scenes.tts: But ganglion cell axons run across that inner surface, toward the optic disk.
scenes.visual: A flat retina from above: ganglion-cell axons sweep in arcs toward the optic disk.
scenes.narration: But ganglion cell axons run across that inner surface, toward the optic disk.

scenes.tts: Predict. Axons from elsewhere run under one electrode. What does the person see when it fires?
scenes.visual: One electrode drops onto the arcs of passing axons. A visual-field inset stays blank.
scenes.narration: Predict. Axons from elsewhere run under one electrode. What does the person see when it fires?

scenes.tts: Often not a dot. Four implant users drew elongated or distorted shapes.
scenes.visual: In the inset, a hand-drawn elongated shape appears. Label: Beyeler and colleagues, 2019; four implant users.
scenes.narration: Often not a dot. Four implant users drew elongated or distorted shapes.

scenes.tts: Each passing axon carries signals from a ganglion cell that reports a different part of the visual field.
scenes.visual: Activity travels along several recruited axons toward the optic disk and on to the brain. A separate inset, labelled modelled visual locations, highlights the places those cells normally report.
scenes.narration: Each passing axon carries signals from a ganglion cell that reports a different part of the visual field.

scenes.tts: Recruit cells along a bundle, and a stretch of visual locations can be activated at once, which can produce a streak.
scenes.visual: In the modelled-locations inset, the highlighted places join into an elongated shape. Label: axon-pathway model, schematic.
scenes.narration: Recruit cells along a bundle, and a stretch of visual locations can be activated at once, which can produce a streak.

scenes.tts: A model of axon pathways accounted for the shapes. It is a model-supported explanation, not a recording.
scenes.visual: A participant-style drawing beside the model's predicted shape. Label: model-supported.
scenes.narration: A model of axon pathways accounted for the shapes. It is a model-supported explanation, not a recording.

scenes.tts: The current reaches neurons whose place on the map is somewhere else.
scenes.visual: The electrode's position and the streak's position marked apart on the map.
scenes.narration: The current reaches neurons whose place on the map is somewhere else.

scenes.tts: So move the electrode away from the axons, and keep each field small. The Prima chip does both.
scenes.caption: So move the electrode away from the axons, and keep each field small. The PRIMA chip does both.
scenes.visual: Cross-section of the retina: axon layer on top; the PRIMA chip sits at the bottom, beneath the retina. Label: subretinal.
scenes.narration: So move the electrode away from the axons, and keep each field small. The PRIMA chip does both.

scenes.tts: Near-infrared light powers its pixels. Each pixel stimulates bipolar cells, and a local return electrode confines its field.
scenes.visual: Near-infrared light shines in; each pixel's field drawn as a small dome held in by a return ring; bipolar cells above light up.
scenes.narration: Near-infrared light powers its pixels. Each pixel stimulates bipolar cells, and a local return electrode confines its field.

scenes.tts: Acuity is scored in log mar. Zero is twenty twenty. One is twenty over two hundred. Higher is worse.
scenes.caption: Acuity is scored in logMAR. 0 is 20/20. 1.0 is 20/200. Higher is worse.
scenes.visual: A logMAR scale from 0 to 2.1, with 20/20 and 20/200 marked. Arrow: higher is worse.
scenes.narration: Acuity is scored in logMAR. 0 is 20/20. 1.0 is 20/200. Higher is worse.

scenes.tts: Predict. Each pixel is a hundred micrometres across. If its field stays within the pixel, what acuity could it give?
scenes.caption: Predict. Each pixel is 100 micrometres across. If its field stays within the pixel, what acuity could it give?
scenes.visual: One 100 micrometre pixel with its confined field. Blank acuity marker on the logMAR scale.
scenes.narration: Predict. Each pixel is 100 micrometres across. If its field stays within the pixel, what acuity could it give?

scenes.tts: The conversion is on screen. The pixel limit is near one point three two log mar, about twenty over four twenty.
scenes.caption: The conversion is on screen. The pixel limit is near 1.32 logMAR, about 20/420.
scenes.visual: On screen: 100 micrometres / 288 micrometres per degree = 0.35 degree = 20.8 arcmin; log of 20.8 = 1.32 logMAR; about 20/420. The marker drops onto the scale at 1.32.
scenes.narration: The conversion is on screen. The pixel limit is near 1.32 logMAR, about 20/420.

scenes.tts: In the Prima vera trial, mean acuity at the implant's own resolution was one point three two log mar.
scenes.caption: In the PRIMAvera trial, mean acuity at the implant's own resolution was 1.32 logMAR.
scenes.visual: A second marker labelled PRIMAvera, native mean, no zoom: 1.32 logMAR, lands on the first. Label: Holz and colleagues.
scenes.narration: In the PRIMAvera trial, mean acuity at the implant's own resolution was 1.32 logMAR.

scenes.tts: The measured mean sits near the pixel limit. Eyes differ in size, so treat it as agreement, not a precise prediction.
scenes.visual: Both markers glow together. Tag on the conversion factor: varies with eye length.
scenes.narration: The measured mean sits near the pixel limit. Eyes differ in size, so treat it as agreement, not a precise prediction.

scenes.tts: For the Argus two, an ideal grid would give about twenty over twenty-four hundred. Yet its best reported grating acuity was about twenty over twelve hundred sixty. So this is an estimate, not a hard limit.
scenes.caption: For the Argus II, an ideal grid would give about 20/2400. Yet its best reported grating acuity was about 20/1260. So this is an estimate, not a hard limit.
scenes.visual: On screen: 575 micrometre spacing = about 2 degrees; nominal static estimate about 20/2400. A second marker, finer on the scale: best reported grating acuity about 20/1260 (Humayun and colleagues, 2012). Tag: nominal estimate, not a limit. No arrow.
scenes.narration: For the Argus II, an ideal grid would give about 20/2400. Yet its best reported grating acuity was about 20/1260. So this is an estimate, not a hard limit.

scenes.tts: Two cautions. A zoomed score adds a magnifier, not pixels. And serious device or procedure related events came with the benefit.
scenes.caption: Two cautions. A zoomed score adds a magnifier, not pixels. And serious device- or procedure-related events came with the benefit.
scenes.visual: A magnifier icon beside the chart: zoom 1 to 12 times. Beside it two columns: benefit, serious adverse events. Label: single-arm, open-label.
scenes.narration: Two cautions. A zoomed score adds a magnifier, not pixels. And serious device- or procedure-related events came with the benefit.

scenes.tts: Optogenetics changes the cells instead. Ganglion cells are made to express a light-gated channel, Chrimson R.
scenes.caption: Optogenetics changes the cells instead. Ganglion cells are made to express a light-gated channel, ChrimsonR.
scenes.visual: Amber-tinted panel: ganglion cells with a light-gated channel in the membrane.
scenes.narration: Optogenetics changes the cells instead. Ganglion cells are made to express a light-gated channel, ChrimsonR.

scenes.tts: Goggles supply the bright amber light, and part of the encoding the retina would have done.
scenes.visual: Goggles project pulses of amber light onto the retina. Label: bright light, plus part of the encoding.
scenes.narration: Goggles supply the bright amber light, and part of the encoding the retina would have done.

scenes.tts: With the goggles, one patient located, counted and touched objects. Without them, the patient did not detect objects.
scenes.visual: Two panels: with goggles, a hand reaching a cup; without goggles, no detection. Label: Sahel and colleagues, 2021; one patient; not normal vision.
scenes.narration: With the goggles, one patient located, counted and touched objects. Without them, the patient did not detect objects.

scenes.tts: Where current reaches the wrong neurons, percepts can be distorted. Prima's mean acuity sits near its pixel limit, as its design aims for. With optogenetics, the goggles' light decides which cells are driven.
scenes.visual: End line on screen: wrong neurons can distort percepts; PRIMA sits near its pixel limit; with optogenetics, the light pattern picks the cells. Tag: not a controlled head-to-head comparison.
scenes.narration: Where current reaches the wrong neurons, percepts can be distorted. PRIMA's mean acuity sits near its pixel limit, as its design aims for. With optogenetics, the goggles' light decides which cells are driven.
scenes.caption: Where current reaches the wrong neurons, percepts can be distorted. PRIMA's mean acuity sits near its pixel limit, as its design aims for. With optogenetics, the goggles' light decides which cells are driven.
